name: Nova
author: Erin Carter
description: A supernova remnant: a bright progenitor star burns off-centre, wreathed in a persistent glowing nebula of turbulent gas and radial filaments, while expanding ragged FBM-torn shells of light are shed continuously and phase-staggered — one always sweeping across the twinkling starfield while another is born and a third dissolves. The shells cycle through the palette as they age, from hot cyan cores to ember red.

params.label: Shell period
params.effect: Seconds per shell-shedding cycle; short values send rings out in rapid succession, long values space them into slow majestic sweeps.

params.label: Ring width
params.effect: Thickness of the expanding shells in CSS pixels, from knife-edge wavefronts to broad luminous bands.

params.label: Filament
params.effect: FBM raggedness of the shell rims: 0 gives clean smooth rings, 1 a torn filamentary remnant.

params.label: Remnant glow
params.effect: Intensity of the persistent nebular gas and radial filaments filling the interior — 0 leaves bare rings on black, 2 a dense luminous remnant.
